10 Two gliders are travelling towards each other on a horizontal air track. Glider P has mass 0.30 kg
and is moving with a constant speed of 1.2 m s–1. Glider Q has mass 0.60 kg and is moving with a
constant speed of 1.8 m s–1.

hints: Notice the directions on the air track diagram: take right as positive so $u_P=+1.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $u_Q=-1.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with masses $0.30\text{ kg}$ and $0.60\text{ kg}$.
Connect the phrase perfectly elastic collision to two rules: total momentum $m_Pu_P+m_Qu_Q=m_Pv_P+m_Qv_Q$ is conserved and speed of approach equals speed of separation.
Set up the two equations with $u_P-u_Q=+3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and total momentum $-0.72\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, then solve for the signed final velocities $v_P$ and $v_Q$ before taking speeds.
walkthrough: Take motion to the right as positive. Then $m_P=0.30\text{ kg}$, $u_P=+1.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $m_Q=0.60\text{ kg}$, $u_Q=-1.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ because the gliders move towards each other.
Total momentum before is $p=m_Pu_P+m_Qu_Q=(0.30)(1.2)+(0.60)(-1.8)=0.36-1.08=-0.72\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$. After collision $0.30v_P+0.60v_Q=-0.72$.

For a perfectly elastic collision the relative speed is unchanged. Speed of approach is $1.2+1.8=3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $u_P-u_Q=-(v_P-v_Q)$, giving $3.0=-(v_P-v_Q)$ or $v_Q-v_P=3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Speeds are magnitudes: P is $2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the left and Q is $0.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the right. This conserves kinetic energy and momentum. This is option C.

A.explanation: Speeds $1.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $0.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ do not conserve total momentum of $-0.72\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$ and do not give separation speed $3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: Speeds $2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $1.4\text{ m s}^{-1}$ give the wrong momentum balance and a separation speed different from the $3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ required for a perfectly elastic impact.

C.explanation: Speeds $2.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for P and $0.2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for Q satisfy both momentum conservation and relative speed $3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for a perfectly elastic collision.

D.explanation: Speeds $3.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $0.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ give too large a total kinetic energy compared with the initial $0.216+0.972=1.188\text{ J}$.
